summary: seapy-ops ships password-gated exfiltration and remote-file-drop channel disguised as a local file utility
details: The package presents itself as a local file-peeker CLI but ships a concealed, password-gated upload mode. When unlocked via a salted-SHA256 password gate (PW_SALT 'seapy::v1::') entered through a no-echo 'ghost typing' prompt, collect_files() recursively walks os.getcwd(), reads every file up to 4MB (skipping only VCS/venv directories), and POSTs the bundle via multipart upload to the hardcoded endpoint https://b196q82k8891-d.space-z.ai/api/cli/upload (also referencing https://preview-chat-960504a9-b4e0-4b69-bc80-6ac3d4fa4ae0.space-z.ai). After upload, the CLI polls /api/cli/status and /api/cli/download, base64-decodes files returned by the server, and writes them under os.getcwd() in a server-chosen subdirectory with no signature, hash, or publisher verification, giving the author's server a channel to drop arbitrary content (including source overwrites) into the developer's project tree, where it will be picked up by the next build or CI run. Code comments explicitly state the surface should 'act like the boring file peeker it pretends to be' when locked, confirming the cover-story design. Startup also imports configuration from ~/.verity, ~/.fpeek, and ~/.pythom into ~/.seapy, and the uninstall path removes binaries by those names from /usr/local/bin and WindowsApps, indicating this package is one of a renamed family of the same operator.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
